source.text: Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Saul now was approving of the killing of him.

en.L: And Saul was approving of his killing.
en.B: Saul, for his part, gave his full approval to Stephen's death.
en.R: Saul agreed that killing Stephen was right.

fr.L: Et Saul approuvait son exécution.
fr.B: Saul, de son côté, approuvait pleinement la mort d’Étienne.
fr.R: Saul était d’accord pour qu’on tue Étienne.

decisions.choice: was approving: went on agreeing with it, sharing in it
decisions.reason: The verb means to approve together with others, to give one's consent. With the past tense of "to be" it describes a settled attitude, not a passing thought. Saul says the same of himself in 22:20.

decisions.choice: this sentence closes the account of Stephen's death
alternatives: the opening of a new account
decisions.reason: Saul was introduced in 7:58, guarding the clothes of the witnesses. This sentence finishes that scene; the next one turns to what followed for the church.

decisions.choice: Stephen
decisions.reason: The chapter begins here, so Balanced and Readable name the man who was killed.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Luke's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("l’eunuque dit", 8:36)
decisions.reason: As in the Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. The imperfect keeps ongoing action ("approuvait", m1). This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ διωγμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις· πάντες δὲ διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων.

records.literal_gloss: There arose then on that the day a persecution great against the church which [was] in Jerusalem; all then were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria except the apostles.

en.L: And on that day there arose a great persecution against the church in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
en.B: That same day a fierce persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and everyone except the apostles was driven out into the country districts of Judea and Samaria.
en.R: On that same day people began to attack the church in Jerusalem very harshly. So all the believers left the city and went to different places in Judea and Samaria. Only the apostles stayed in Jerusalem.

fr.L: Et en ce jour-là, il s’éleva une grande persécution contre l’église qui [était] à Jérusalem, et tous furent dispersés dans les régions de la Judée et de la Samarie, excepté les apôtres.
fr.B: Ce jour-là même, une violente persécution se déchaîna contre l’église de Jérusalem, et tous, sauf les apôtres, furent dispersés dans les campagnes de Judée et de Samarie.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, des gens ont commencé à attaquer très durement l’église de Jérusalem. Alors tous les croyants ont quitté la ville et sont partis dans différents endroits de Judée et de Samarie. Seuls les apôtres sont restés à Jérusalem.

decisions.choice: persecution: hostile pursuit and harassment of a group
decisions.reason: The word means to pursue someone in order to harm them. Luke shows what it involved in 8:3: houses searched, men and women dragged off to prison.

decisions.choice: all: the believers in general, said broadly
decisions.reason: Luke speaks broadly. There are still believers in Jerusalem in 9:26-28, and Saul goes on finding people there to arrest (8:3).

decisions.choice: Judea and Samaria: the second stage of the witness Jesus foretold
decisions.reason: Jesus told the apostles they would be his witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth (1:8). The persecution carries the word into the second of these.

decisions.choice: except the apostles: the Twelve stayed in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Luke does not say why they stayed. The apostles are in Jerusalem in 8:14, and they send Peter and John from there.

decisions.choice: people began to attack the church very harshly
decisions.reason: Readable says what a persecution is in plain words.

decisions.choice: all the believers left the city; only the apostles stayed
alternatives: all were scattered except the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names who "all" are and says the apostles stayed, which "except" implies.

decisions.choice: l’église (lowercase) for the believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As the style guide settles it: the capital is for the whole body of believers, the lowercase for one congregation, here the church in Jerusalem.

source.text: συνεκόμισαν δὲ τὸν Στέφανον ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ ἐποίησαν κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Buried now the Stephen men devout and made lamentation great over him.

en.L: And devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him.
en.B: Some devout men gave Stephen a burial and mourned loudly for him.
en.R: Some men who loved God buried Stephen. They cried and wept loudly because he had died.

fr.L: Et des hommes pieux ensevelirent Étienne et firent sur lui de grandes lamentations.
fr.B: Des hommes pieux donnèrent une sépulture à Étienne et le pleurèrent à grands cris.
fr.R: Des hommes qui aimaient Dieu ont enterré Étienne. Ils ont pleuré et se sont lamentés très fort parce qu’il était mort.

decisions.choice: devout men: men who feared God, perhaps Jews who were not believers
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same word for the devout Jews in Jerusalem at Pentecost (2:5) and for Simeon (Luke 2:25). It may mean believers, or devout Jews who honored Stephen; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: lamentation: loud public mourning, with weeping and beating the breast
decisions.reason: The word means beating the breast in grief, as mourners did for the dead (Luke 8:52, 23:27). Mourning so openly for a man stoned by the council was a bold act.

decisions.choice: men who loved God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "devout" means in common words.

source.text: Σαῦλος δὲ ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους εἰσπορευόμενος, σύρων τε ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν.

records.literal_gloss: Saul however was ravaging the church, house after house entering, dragging off both men and women he was handing over to prison.

en.L: But Saul was ravaging the church, entering house after house, and dragging off both men and women, he was handing [them] over to prison.
en.B: Saul, however, set about destroying the church. He went from house to house, hauled off men and women alike, and had them put in prison.
en.R: But Saul tried to destroy the church. He went into one house after another. He dragged out men and women who believed in Jesus and threw them into prison.

fr.L: Mais Saul ravageait l’église : entrant dans les maisons l’une après l’autre et traînant hommes et femmes, il [les] livrait à la prison.
fr.B: Saul, lui, s’acharnait à détruire l’église. Il allait de maison en maison, en arrachait hommes et femmes et les faisait jeter en prison.
fr.R: Mais Saul a essayé de détruire l’église. Il entrait dans une maison après l’autre. Il traînait dehors les hommes et les femmes qui croyaient en Jésus, et il les jetait en prison.

decisions.choice: was ravaging: was laying waste, trying to destroy
decisions.reason: The verb is used of wild animals mauling, or of armies laying a land waste. The tense shows that he kept doing it. Paul says the same of himself in Galatians 1:13: he tried to destroy the church.

decisions.choice: house after house: the homes where the believers met
decisions.reason: The believers gathered in homes (2:46, 5:42, 12:12). Saul searched them one by one.

decisions.choice: both men and women: no one was spared because she was a woman
decisions.reason: Luke names women as well as men among those arrested, as Paul does in 22:4.

decisions.choice: who believed in Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says who the people were, as the context makes clear.

source.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον.

records.literal_gloss: Those indeed therefore having been scattered went about proclaiming the good news, the word.

en.L: Those then who had been scattered went about proclaiming the good news of the word.
en.B: Those who had been scattered went from place to place, announcing the good news of the message.
en.R: The believers who had left Jerusalem traveled from place to place. Everywhere they went, they told people the good news about Jesus.

fr.L: Ceux donc qui avaient été dispersés allèrent de lieu en lieu, annonçant la bonne nouvelle de la parole.
fr.B: Ceux qui avaient été dispersés passaient d’un endroit à l’autre en annonçant la bonne nouvelle du message.
fr.R: Les croyants qui avaient quitté Jérusalem sont allés d’un endroit à l’autre. Partout où ils passaient, ils annonçaient aux gens la bonne nouvelle au sujet de Jésus.

decisions.choice: proclaiming the word as good news: announcing the message about Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb means to announce good news. "The word" is the message about Jesus, as in 4:31 and 6:4. Those who were scattered were ordinary believers, not only the apostles.

decisions.choice: then: the scattering led to the spreading of the word
alternatives: no link with what came before
decisions.reason: The paired particles tie this sentence to the scattering in 8:1. Luke shows that the persecution meant to stop the message spread it instead. 11:19 picks up the same thread with the same words.

decisions.choice: the good news about Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the word" was, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: annoncer la bonne nouvelle
decisions.reason: The verb is about announcing good news (m1). "Évangéliser" is church language and today suggests organised mission; "annoncer la bonne nouvelle" says what the word says at every level and is used for this verb through the chapter.

source.text: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν χριστόν.

records.literal_gloss: Philip now having gone down to the city of Samaria was proclaiming to them the Christ.

en.L: And Philip, having gone down to the city of Samaria, was proclaiming the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to them.
en.B: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and began to proclaim the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to the people there.
en.R: Philip went to the main city of Samaria. He told the people there about the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the King God had promised.

fr.L: Et Philippe, étant descendu dans la ville de Samarie, leur proclamait le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Philippe descendit dans la ville de Samarie et se mit à y proclamer le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} aux habitants.
fr.R: Philippe est allé dans la ville principale de Samarie. Il a parlé aux gens de là-bas du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le Roi que Dieu avait promis.

decisions.choice: Philip: one of the Seven, not Philip the apostle
decisions.reason: The apostles stayed in Jerusalem (8:1), and they send Peter and John to Samaria later (8:14). Philip was chosen with Stephen to serve the widows (6:5). He is later called "Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven" (21:8).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the city of Samaria"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the article ("the city"), and the SBLGNT follows them; others lack it ("a city"). With the article, it is most likely the chief city of the region, called Samaria in the Old Testament and rebuilt by Herod as Sebaste. Without it, any town of the region. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the region between Judea and Galilee, home of the Samaritans
decisions.reason: The Samaritans worshiped the God of Israel and kept the five books of Moses, but on Mount Gerizim, not in Jerusalem (John 4:9, 4:20). Jews and Samaritans had long been hostile.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's promised anointed King
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title. The Samaritans too were waiting for a Messiah (John 4:25).

decisions.choice: the main city of Samaria
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading with the article, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the King God had promised
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title once.

source.text: προσεῖχον δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·

records.literal_gloss: Were paying attention now the crowds to the things being spoken by Philip with one mind in the hearing them and seeing the signs that he was doing.

en.L: And the crowds with one mind were paying attention to the things spoken by Philip, as they heard and saw the signs that he was doing.
en.B: The crowds, one and all, listened closely to what Philip said, as they heard him and saw the signs he performed.
en.R: Crowds of people listened carefully to what Philip said. They all heard him, and they saw the signs he did, the miracles that showed God's power.

fr.L: Et les foules, d’un même cœur, étaient attentives à ce que disait Philippe, lorsqu’elles entendaient et voyaient les signes qu’il faisait.
fr.B: Les foules, unanimes, écoutaient avec attention ce que disait Philippe, car elles l’entendaient et voyaient les signes qu’il accomplissait.
fr.R: Des foules de gens ont écouté avec attention ce que Philippe disait. Tous l’entendaient, et ils voyaient les signes qu’il faisait, les miracles qui montraient la puissance de Dieu.

decisions.choice: were paying attention: listened and took to heart
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn one's mind to something. It is used of the same people's attention to Simon in 8:10-11; now they turn to Philip.

decisions.choice: with one mind: all alike, together
decisions.reason: The word describes a group acting as one, as the believers do in 1:14 and 2:46.

decisions.choice: signs: miracles that point to God at work
decisions.reason: A sign is a deed that shows something. Luke lists what they were in 8:7.

decisions.choice: the miracles that showed God's power
decisions.reason: Readable says what the signs were and what they showed.

source.text: πολλοὶ γὰρ τῶν ἐχόντων πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα βοῶντα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξήρχοντο, πολλοὶ δὲ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν·

records.literal_gloss: Many for of those having spirits unclean, crying with voice loud they were coming out, many now having been paralyzed and lame were healed.

en.L: For [from] many of those who had unclean spirits, they were coming out, crying with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
en.B: Unclean spirits came out of many people, shrieking as they left, and many who were paralyzed or lame were healed.
en.R: Many people had evil spirits in them. The spirits screamed loudly as they came out of them. And many people who could not move or walk were healed.

fr.L: Car de beaucoup de ceux qui avaient des esprits impurs, [ces esprits] sortaient en criant d’une voix forte, et beaucoup de paralysés et de boiteux furent guéris.
fr.B: Des esprits impurs sortirent de beaucoup de gens en poussant de grands cris, et beaucoup de paralysés et de boiteux furent guéris.
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens avaient en eux des esprits mauvais. Ces esprits criaient très fort en sortant d’eux. Et beaucoup de gens qui ne pouvaient ni bouger ni marcher ont été guéris.

decisions.choice: the spirits came out of many who had them
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with the people and then makes the spirits the subject of "were coming out". The crying out belongs to the spirits, as in Luke 4:33-35 and 4:41.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
alternatives: unclean in the sense of unwashed
decisions.reason: Luke uses "unclean spirit" and "demon" for the same beings (Luke 4:33, 8:29). They are unclean because they are opposed to God's holiness.

decisions.choice: paralyzed and lame: unable to move limbs, unable to walk
decisions.reason: Two groups are named: those who were paralyzed, and those whose legs or feet were crippled, like the man in 3:2.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word, as in earlier chapters; the meaning note explains "unclean".

decisions.choice: could not move or walk
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two conditions were.

decisions.choice: des esprits impurs (L, B); des esprits mauvais (R)
decisions.reason: "Esprit impur" is the term the style guide settles for the New Testament; "immonde" is dated. Readable follows the English "evil spirits".

source.text: ἐγένετο δὲ πολλὴ χαρὰ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: There was then great joy in the city that.

en.L: And there was great joy in that city.
en.B: So there was great joy in that city.
en.R: The people of that city were filled with joy.

fr.L: Et il y eut une grande joie dans cette ville-là.
fr.B: Aussi y eut-il une grande joie dans cette ville.
fr.R: Les gens de cette ville ont été remplis de joie.

decisions.choice: joy: the gladness that comes with salvation
decisions.reason: Joy often follows the coming of the good news in Luke and Acts (Luke 2:10, Acts 8:39, 13:52, 16:34).

decisions.choice: the people of that city
decisions.reason: Readable names the people whose joy it was.

source.text: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ὀνόματι Σίμων προϋπῆρχεν ἐν τῇ πόλει μαγεύων καὶ ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν, ᾧ προσεῖχον πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ Δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ καλουμένη Μεγάλη.

records.literal_gloss: A man now certain by name Simon was before in the city practicing magic and amazing the people of Samaria, saying to be someone himself great, \v 10 to whom were paying attention all from small to great saying, This one is the power of God that called Great.

en.L: Now a certain man named Simon had been in the city before, practicing magic and amazing the people of Samaria, saying that he himself was someone great, \v 10 to whom all paid attention, from small to great, saying, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
en.B: Now there was a man named Simon who had been in the city for some time, working magic and astonishing the people of Samaria. He made himself out to be someone great, \v 10 and everyone, from the least to the most important, hung on his words. "This man," they said, "is the power of God that is called Great."
en.R: A man named Simon had lived in that city for some time. He did magic and amazed the people of Samaria. He said that he was someone great. \v 10 Everyone listened to him, both poor people and important people. They said, "This man is the power of God that people call the Great Power."

fr.L: Or un certain homme du nom de Simon se trouvait auparavant dans la ville, pratiquant la magie et stupéfiant le peuple de la Samarie, se disant quelqu’un de grand, \v 10 lui à qui tous étaient attentifs, du petit jusqu’au grand, disant : « Celui-ci est la puissance de Dieu, celle qu’on appelle la Grande. »
fr.B: Or il y avait dans la ville, depuis un certain temps, un homme nommé Simon, qui pratiquait la magie et frappait de stupeur le peuple de Samarie. Il se faisait passer pour quelqu’un de grand, \v 10 et tous, du plus petit au plus grand, étaient suspendus à ses lèvres. « Cet homme, disaient-ils, est la puissance de Dieu, celle qu’on appelle la Grande. »
fr.R: Un homme appelé Simon vivait dans cette ville depuis quelque temps. Il faisait de la magie et il étonnait beaucoup les habitants de la Samarie. Il disait qu’il était quelqu’un de grand. \v 10 Tout le monde l’écoutait, les pauvres comme les gens importants. Ils disaient : « Cet homme est la puissance de Dieu, celle qu’on appelle la Grande Puissance. »

decisions.choice: practicing magic: working spells and wonders by occult arts
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the name of the Persian magi and came to mean practicing sorcery. Luke tells of another such man, Elymas, in 13:6-11.

decisions.choice: amazing: astonishing, carrying them away
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone out of their senses with amazement. The same verb is used of Simon himself in 8:13, when he is amazed at Philip's signs.

decisions.choice: from small to great: everyone, from the least to the most important
decisions.reason: The phrase covers every rank of people, as in Hebrews 8:11.

decisions.choice: the power of God that is called Great: a title naming Simon as a divine power
alternatives: simply a man with great power
decisions.reason: "Great" seems to have been a title, perhaps for the highest god or for a power that came from him. The people say Simon is that power in human form. The exact sense of the title is not known.

decisions.choice: that people call the Great Power
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "Great" is a name or title.

decisions.choice: hung on his words
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an English idiom for listening closely, which the verb means here.

decisions.choice: étaient suspendus à ses lèvres
decisions.reason: French has an idiom for listening closely that matches the English "hung on his words" and the force of the verb here.

source.text: προσεῖχον δὲ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: They were paying attention now to him because of the for a long time with the magic arts to have amazed them.

en.L: And they paid attention to him because for a long time he had amazed them with [his] magic arts.
en.B: They followed him because for a long while he had dazzled them with his magic.
en.R: They followed him because he had amazed them with his magic for a long time.

fr.L: Et ils étaient attentifs à lui, parce que depuis longtemps il les avait stupéfiés par [ses] pratiques de magie.
fr.B: Ils le suivaient parce que depuis longtemps il les éblouissait par sa magie.
fr.R: Ils le suivaient parce que, depuis longtemps, il les étonnait avec sa magie.

decisions.choice: were paying attention: followed him, gave him their loyalty
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:6 and 8:10. The tense shows a lasting attachment.

decisions.choice: because: his long run of wonders was the reason for their loyalty
decisions.reason: The construction gives the cause. Philip's signs (8:6) now draw them away from Simon's magic.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες.

records.literal_gloss: When however they believed Philip proclaiming the good news concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were being baptized, men both and women.

en.L: But when they believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, they were baptized, both men and women.
en.B: But when Philip announced the good news of God's kingdom and of the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, they believed him, and both men and women were baptized.
en.R: Philip told them the good news about God's kingdom and about Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. The people believed what Philip said, and they were baptized, both men and women.

fr.L: Mais quand ils crurent Philippe, qui annonçait la bonne nouvelle au sujet du royaume de Dieu et du nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, ils furent baptisés, hommes et femmes.
fr.B: Mais quand Philippe annonça la bonne nouvelle du royaume de Dieu et du nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, ils le crurent, et des hommes comme des femmes se firent baptiser.
fr.R: Philippe leur a annoncé la bonne nouvelle du royaume de Dieu et de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Les gens ont cru ce que Philippe disait, et ils ont été baptisés, hommes et femmes.

decisions.choice: they believed Philip: they accepted his message as true
alternatives: they trusted Philip as a person
decisions.reason: The verb with a person means to believe what that person says. What they believed was his message about the kingdom and Jesus.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: God's rule, which Jesus proclaimed
alternatives: a place or a political realm
decisions.reason: The phrase that summed up Jesus's own preaching (Luke 4:43) also sums up the message of his witnesses (1:3, 19:8, 28:31).

decisions.choice: the name of Jesus Christ: Jesus himself, his person and authority
alternatives: only the name as a word
decisions.reason: As in 3:16 and 4:12, the name stands for the person.

decisions.choice: they were being baptized: one after another, as each believed
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense suggests baptisms that went on over time.

decisions.choice: Philip's preaching first, then their belief
decisions.reason: Readable puts the events in the order they happened and breaks the sentence up.

decisions.choice: le royaume de Dieu at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for the New Testament. English Balanced and Readable say "God's kingdom"; French keeps the one phrase, which is already plain.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Σίμων καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν, καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ, θεωρῶν τε σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας γινομένας ἐξίστατο.

records.literal_gloss: The and Simon also himself believed, and having been baptized he was continuing with Philip, seeing then signs and miracles great happening he was amazed.

en.L: And Simon himself also believed, and having been baptized, he was continuing with Philip; and seeing signs and great miracles taking place, he was amazed.
en.B: Even Simon himself believed, and after he was baptized he stayed close to Philip. When he saw the signs and great miracles that were happening, he was astounded.
en.R: Simon also believed, and he was baptized. After that he stayed with Philip everywhere he went. Simon saw the signs and the great miracles that Philip did, and he was amazed.

fr.L: Et Simon lui-même crut aussi, et, ayant été baptisé, il s’attachait à Philippe ; et, voyant des signes et de grands miracles se produire, il était stupéfait.
fr.B: Simon lui-même crut, lui aussi, et après avoir été baptisé, il ne quittait plus Philippe. En voyant les signes et les grands miracles qui se produisaient, il était frappé de stupeur.
fr.R: Simon aussi a cru, et il a été baptisé. Après cela, il est resté avec Philippe partout où celui-ci allait. Simon voyait les signes et les grands miracles que Philippe faisait, et il était très étonné.

decisions.choice: believed: Simon professed faith and was baptized, but his heart was not right (8:21)
alternatives: Simon's belief was full and sincere
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same verb as for the others in 8:12. But 8:18-23 shows that Simon still thought of God's gift as a power to buy. Luke does not say whether his belief was real but immature or only on the surface.

decisions.choice: continuing with: staying close to, attaching himself to
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold fast to someone or something, as the believers held fast to prayer (1:14, 2:42).

decisions.choice: he was amazed: the same verb used of the effect of his own magic (8:9, 8:11)
decisions.reason: Simon had amazed others; now he is amazed himself.

decisions.choice: that Philip did
decisions.reason: Readable names who did the miracles, as 8:6 says.

decisions.choice: stupéfait (L), frappé de stupeur (B), très étonné (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the word it used for the effect of Simon's magic in 8:9 and 8:11, so that the reader sees the same verb turned back on him (m3).

source.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀπόστολοι ὅτι δέδεκται ἡ Σαμάρεια τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτοὺς Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην, οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν πνεῦμα ἅγιον·

records.literal_gloss: Having heard now the in Jerusalem apostles that had received Samaria the word of God, they sent to them Peter and John, \v 15 who having come down prayed for them so that they might receive Spirit Holy;

en.L: Now when the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them, \v 15 who, having come down, prayed for them so that they might receive [the] Holy Spirit;
en.B: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them. \v 15 The two went down and prayed for the people there to receive the Holy Spirit,
en.R: The apostles in Jerusalem heard that the people of Samaria had accepted God's message. So they sent Peter and John to them. \v 15 When Peter and John arrived, they prayed for the believers in Samaria. They asked God to give them the Holy Spirit.

fr.L: Or les apôtres [qui étaient] à Jérusalem, ayant appris que la Samarie avait reçu la parole de Dieu, leur envoyèrent Pierre et Jean, \v 15 qui, étant descendus, prièrent pour eux afin qu’ils reçoivent l’Esprit Saint ;
fr.B: Quand les apôtres qui étaient à Jérusalem apprirent que la Samarie avait accueilli la parole de Dieu, ils leur envoyèrent Pierre et Jean. \v 15 Arrivés là-bas, ceux-ci prièrent pour que les gens reçoivent l’Esprit Saint,
fr.R: Les apôtres de Jérusalem ont appris que les gens de Samarie avaient accepté le message de Dieu. Alors ils leur ont envoyé Pierre et Jean. \v 15 Quand Pierre et Jean sont arrivés, ils ont prié pour les croyants de Samarie. Ils ont demandé à Dieu de leur donner l’Esprit Saint.

decisions.choice: Samaria had received the word of God: the people of Samaria had accepted the message
decisions.reason: Luke names the region for its people. To receive the word is to accept it in faith, as in 2:41 and 11:1.

decisions.choice: they sent Peter and John: the apostles in Jerusalem took part in the new work
alternatives: they were sent to check on Philip
decisions.reason: Luke does not give the reason for sending them. The same thing happens when the word reaches Antioch (11:22). Peter and John had worked together before (3:1, 4:13).

decisions.choice: so that they might receive: the purpose of their prayer
decisions.reason: The conjunction gives the aim. Verse 17 tells that it came about.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 8:16, which gives the reason for the prayer
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends this record with a raised dot. Verse 16 explains why they prayed: the Spirit had not yet come upon any of them.

decisions.choice: they asked God to give them
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom they prayed and what they asked.

decisions.choice: l’Esprit Saint
decisions.reason: The style guide's term, as in John and Hebrews. The Greek has no article here; French needs one, so Literal writes it without brackets.

source.text: οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπ’ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός, μόνον δὲ βεβαπτισμένοι ὑπῆρχον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not yet for was upon any of them fallen, only however having been baptized they were into the name of the Lord Jesus.

en.L: For [the Spirit] had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had only been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
en.B: for the Spirit had not yet come down on any of them. They had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
en.R: The Holy Spirit had not yet come on any of them. They had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

fr.L: Car [l’Esprit] n’était encore tombé sur aucun d’eux ; ils avaient seulement été baptisés dans le nom du Seigneur Jésus.
fr.B: car l’Esprit n’était encore descendu sur aucun d’eux. Ils avaient seulement été baptisés au nom du Seigneur Jésus.
fr.R: L’Esprit Saint n’était encore venu sur aucun d’eux. Ils avaient seulement été baptisés au nom du Seigneur Jésus.

decisions.choice: had not yet fallen upon: the Spirit had not yet come on them as at Pentecost
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same picture for the Spirit coming on Cornelius's household (10:44, 11:15). He does not say why the gift was delayed in Samaria. One reading sees God joining the Samaritans to the apostles' work in Jerusalem, so that the long divide between the two peoples would not carry into the church; but the text does not explain it.

decisions.choice: baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus: baptized as belonging to Jesus
decisions.reason: "Into the name" marks to whom the baptized now belong. Compare 2:38 and 19:5.

decisions.choice: the Spirit
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject; it is the Holy Spirit of 8:15. English names him rather than using a pronoun.

decisions.choice: dans le nom (L); au nom (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the preposition of movement ("into the name"), which says that they now belonged to Jesus (m2); Balanced and Readable use the usual French "baptisés au nom de".

source.text: τότε ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτούς, καὶ ἐλάμβανον πνεῦμα ἅγιον.

records.literal_gloss: Then they were laying the hands on them, and they were receiving Spirit Holy.

en.L: Then they laid [their] hands on them, and they received [the] Holy Spirit.
en.B: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
en.R: Then Peter and John put their hands on the believers, and they received the Holy Spirit.

fr.L: Alors ils leur imposaient les mains, et ils recevaient l’Esprit Saint.
fr.B: Alors Pierre et Jean leur imposèrent les mains, et ils reçurent l’Esprit Saint.
fr.R: Alors Pierre et Jean ont posé les mains sur les croyants, et ceux-ci ont reçu l’Esprit Saint.

decisions.choice: laying on hands: a sign of prayer and blessing for a person
alternatives: a means that works by itself
decisions.reason: Laying on hands goes with prayer in 6:6 and 13:3. In 9:17 Ananias, not an apostle, lays hands on Saul, who is then filled with the Spirit; in 10:44 the Spirit comes with no laying on of hands.

decisions.choice: were laying, were receiving: one after another
decisions.reason: Both verbs are imperfect, which suggests the apostles went from one person to the next.

decisions.choice: Peter and John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Σίμων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων δίδοται τὸ πνεῦμα προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα λέγων· Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ πνεῦμα ἅγιον.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen now the Simon that through the laying on of the hands of the apostles is given the Spirit, he offered them money \v 19 saying, Give also to me the authority this, that on whom if I lay the hands, he may receive Spirit Holy.

en.L: Now when Simon saw that through the laying on of the apostles' hands the Spirit was given, he offered them money, \v 19 saying, "Give me also this authority, so that anyone on whom I lay [my] hands may receive [the] Holy Spirit."
en.B: Simon saw that the Spirit was given when the apostles laid their hands on people, and he offered them money. \v 19 "Let me have this power too," he said, "so that whoever I place my hands on will receive the Holy Spirit."
en.R: Simon saw that the Spirit came to people when the apostles put their hands on them. So he offered Peter and John money. \v 19 He said, "Give me this power too. Then when I put my hands on someone, that person will receive the Holy Spirit."

fr.L: Or Simon, ayant vu que par l’imposition des mains des apôtres l’Esprit était donné, leur offrit de l’argent, \v 19 disant : « Donnez-moi, à moi aussi, cette autorité, afin que celui à qui j’imposerai les mains reçoive l’Esprit Saint. »
fr.B: Simon vit que l’Esprit était donné quand les apôtres imposaient les mains, et il leur offrit de l’argent. \v 19 « Donnez-moi ce pouvoir, à moi aussi, dit-il, pour que celui à qui j’imposerai les mains reçoive l’Esprit Saint. »
fr.R: Simon a vu que l’Esprit venait sur les gens quand les apôtres posaient les mains sur eux. Alors il a offert de l’argent à Pierre et à Jean. \v 19 Il leur a dit : « Donnez-moi ce pouvoir, à moi aussi. Alors, quand je poserai les mains sur quelqu’un, cette personne recevra l’Esprit Saint. »

decisions.choice: Simon saw: the coming of the Spirit could be seen
decisions.reason: Luke does not describe what Simon saw. At Pentecost the Spirit's coming could be seen and heard (2:33), and in 10:46 people speak in tongues.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and power to do something
decisions.reason: The word is used for the authority Jesus gave the Twelve (Luke 9:1). Simon thinks of it as something that can be passed on for a price.

decisions.choice: he offered money: he tried to buy a spiritual power
alternatives: he offered a gift for the poor
decisions.reason: Magicians in the Greek world sold and bought spells and secret knowledge. Simon's name later gave its name to the buying and selling of church offices.

decisions.choice: power
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "power", since Simon is asking for the ability to give the Spirit, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Peter and John
decisions.reason: Readable names the apostles who were there.

source.text: Πέτρος δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Τὸ ἀργύριόν σου σὺν σοὶ εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: Peter however said to him, The silver of you with you may it be to destruction, because the gift of God you thought through money to obtain.

en.L: But Peter said to him, "May your silver go with you to destruction, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money.
en.B: Peter answered him, "To ruin with you and your silver! You thought you could get the gift of God with money.
en.R: But Peter said to him, "May you and your money both be destroyed! You thought that you could buy God's gift with money.

fr.L: Mais Pierre lui dit : « Que ton argent aille avec toi à la perdition, parce que tu as cru pouvoir acquérir le don de Dieu avec de l’argent.
fr.B: Pierre lui répondit : « À la ruine, toi et ton argent ! Tu as cru pouvoir obtenir le don de Dieu avec de l’argent.
fr.R: Mais Pierre lui a dit : « Que tu sois détruit, toi et ton argent ! Tu as pensé que tu pouvais acheter le don de Dieu avec de l’argent.

decisions.choice: may your silver go with you to destruction: a curse on Simon and his money
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form used for wishes. Peter calls down ruin on Simon together with his money. In 8:22 he urges him to repent, so the curse is a warning, not a closed door.

decisions.choice: destruction: ruin, perishing before God
decisions.reason: The word is often used of final ruin (Matthew 7:13, Philippians 3:19).

decisions.choice: the gift of God: the Holy Spirit, given freely
alternatives: the power to give the Spirit
decisions.reason: Peter calls the Spirit "the gift" in 2:38, and so does Luke in 10:45 and 11:17. A gift cannot be bought.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: Silver coins were the common money. Simon offered "money" (8:18).

decisions.choice: To ruin with you and your silver!
alternatives: May your silver perish with you
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the curse its force as a short exclamation.

decisions.choice: ton argent
decisions.reason: French "argent" means both silver and money, so the one word carries the Greek "silver" and its sense "money" (m4) without a choice between them.

source.text: οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου οὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not is to you part nor lot in the matter this, the for heart of you not is right before God.

en.L: You have no part or share in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
en.B: You have no part or portion in this, because in God's eyes your heart is not right.
en.R: You have no place in this work of God. You do not have a right heart in God's sight.

fr.L: Tu n’as pas de part ni de lot en cette affaire, car ton cœur n’est pas droit en face de Dieu.
fr.B: Tu n’as aucune part ni aucune place dans tout cela, car aux yeux de Dieu ton cœur n’est pas droit.
fr.R: Tu n’as pas de place dans cette œuvre de Dieu. Ton cœur n’est pas droit aux yeux de Dieu.

decisions.choice: part nor lot: the words used of the Levites, who had no share in the land
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses the same pair of words in Deuteronomy 12:12 and 14:27. "Lot" is also the word for the place in the ministry that fell to Matthias (1:17, 1:25).

decisions.choice: this matter: this gift and the work it belongs to
decisions.reason: The word can mean "word" or "message", and some read "you have no share in this message". Here it most likely means the matter at hand, the giving of the Spirit.

decisions.choice: your heart is not right before God: the words of Psalm 78:37
decisions.reason: In the Greek of Psalm 78:37 (77:37 in that numbering) Israel's heart was not right with God. The phrase means a heart not true or upright toward God.

decisions.choice: no place in this work of God
alternatives: no part or share in this matter
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two words for a share into one plain phrase.

source.text: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας σου ταύτης, καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σου·

records.literal_gloss: Repent therefore from the wickedness of you this and pray to the Lord, if perhaps will be forgiven you the intent of the heart of you;

en.L: So repent of this wickedness of yours and pray to the Lord, if perhaps the intent of your heart will be forgiven you,
en.B: So turn from this wickedness of yours and pray to the Lord. It may be that he will forgive you for what you had in your heart,
en.R: So stop doing this evil thing and turn back to God. Pray to the Lord. Maybe he will forgive you for what you were planning in your heart.

fr.L: Repens-toi donc de cette méchanceté qui est la tienne, et prie le Seigneur : peut-être l’intention de ton cœur te sera-t-elle pardonnée,
fr.B: Repens-toi donc de cette méchanceté et prie le Seigneur. Il se peut qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te pardonne ce que tu avais dans le cœur,
fr.R: Arrête de faire ce mal et reviens vers Dieu. Prie le Seigneur. Peut-être qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te pardonnera ce que tu préparais dans ton cœur.

decisions.choice: repent: turn away from it, change one's mind and ways
decisions.reason: The word means a change of mind that leads to a change of life, as in 2:38 and 3:19.

decisions.choice: if perhaps: forgiveness is not presumed, but it is possible
decisions.reason: The words express real uncertainty about the outcome, but Peter still urges Simon to pray. The doubt lies in Simon's heart, not in God's willingness.

decisions.choice: the Lord: here most likely God
decisions.reason: "Lord" can mean God or Jesus in Acts. Some manuscripts read "God" here. The same Lord is meant in 8:24.

decisions.choice: intent: plan, purpose, what one has in mind
decisions.reason: The word means a thought one has formed or a design. Simon's plan was to buy the Spirit.

decisions.choice: stop doing this evil thing and turn back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what it means to repent.

decisions.choice: se repentir (L, B); arrête de faire ce mal et reviens vers Dieu (R)
alternatives: détourne-toi de cette méchanceté (B), as the English "turn from"
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "se repentir" at Literal and Balanced for the whole New Testament; Readable explains it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} for the Lord who may forgive (and "Demandez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}" in 8:24)
decisions.reason: The English has no setting on this "he"; the Lord here is most likely God (m3), so French gives the pronoun the deity setting, as it does for every pronoun for God.

source.text: εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄντα.

records.literal_gloss: In for gall of bitterness and bond of unrighteousness I see you being.

en.L: For I see that you are in [the] gall of bitterness and [the] bond of unrighteousness."
en.B: For I can see that you are full of bitter poison and bound by wrongdoing."
en.R: I can see that you are full of bitter jealousy. You are a prisoner of your sin."

fr.L: Car je vois que tu es dans le fiel de l’amertume et le lien de l’injustice. »
fr.B: Car je le vois : tu es rempli d’un poison amer et prisonnier du mal. »
fr.R: Je vois que tu es plein d’une jalousie amère. Tu es prisonnier de ton péché. »

decisions.choice: gall of bitterness: bitter poison, a root of evil, as in Deuteronomy 29:18
decisions.reason: Gall was a bitter, poisonous herb. In the Greek of Deuteronomy 29:18 (29:17 in that numbering) Moses warns against anyone whose heart turns from God, a root bearing gall and bitterness. Hebrews 12:15 uses the same picture.

decisions.choice: bond of unrighteousness: held captive by wrongdoing
alternatives: himself a bond that holds others
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that Simon is bound by sin, or that he is a bundle of wrongdoing. Isaiah 58:6 in Greek uses the same words for bonds of injustice to be loosed.

decisions.choice: you are in: the phrase describes the state Simon is in
decisions.reason: The preposition with "being" describes a state. Some read it as Simon's coming destiny, but the verb "I see" speaks of the present.

decisions.choice: bitter jealousy
decisions.reason: Readable names the bitterness Simon shows, the wish to have what the apostles had. It explains the picture rather than keeping it.

decisions.choice: a prisoner of your sin
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading that Simon is bound by sin.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Σίμων εἶπεν· Δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν κύριον ὅπως μηδὲν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε.

records.literal_gloss: Answering now the Simon said, Pray you on behalf of me to the Lord, so that nothing may come upon me of which you have spoken.

en.L: And Simon answered and said, "You pray to the Lord on my behalf, so that nothing of what you have spoken may come upon me."
en.B: Simon replied, "Pray to the Lord for me yourselves, so that none of the things you have said will happen to me."
en.R: Simon answered, "Please pray to the Lord for me. Ask him not to let these terrible things happen to me."

fr.L: Et Simon, répondant, dit : « Vous, priez le Seigneur pour moi, afin que rien de ce que vous avez dit ne vienne sur moi. »
fr.B: Simon répondit : « Priez vous-mêmes le Seigneur pour moi, afin que rien de ce que vous avez dit ne m’arrive. »
fr.R: Simon a répondu : « S’il vous plaît, priez le Seigneur pour moi. Demandez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de ne pas laisser ces choses terribles m’arriver. »

decisions.choice: you pray: Simon asks the apostles to pray, rather than praying himself
decisions.reason: Peter told Simon to pray (8:22). Simon answers with the plural pronoun stressed: you pray for me. Luke does not tell what became of him.

decisions.choice: what you have spoken: the destruction Peter spoke of in 8:20
decisions.reason: Simon fears the curse, not the sin Peter named.

decisions.choice: these terrible things
decisions.reason: Readable sums up what Peter had said would happen.

source.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου ὑπέστρεφον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν εὐηγγελίζοντο.

records.literal_gloss: They indeed therefore having testified and having spoken the word of the Lord were returning to Jerusalem, many and villages of the Samaritans they were proclaiming the good news.

en.L: So they, having testified and spoken the word of the Lord, were returning to Jerusalem, and they were proclaiming the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.
en.B: After Peter and John had borne witness and spoken the word of the Lord, they set out back to Jerusalem, announcing the good news in many Samaritan villages on the way.
en.R: Peter and John told people what they knew about Jesus, and they spoke the word of the Lord. Then they went back to Jerusalem. On the way they told the good news in many villages in Samaria.

fr.L: Eux donc, ayant rendu témoignage et ayant annoncé la parole du Seigneur, retournaient à Jérusalem, et ils annonçaient la bonne nouvelle à beaucoup de villages des Samaritains.
fr.B: Après avoir rendu témoignage et annoncé la parole du Seigneur, Pierre et Jean reprirent le chemin de Jérusalem, en annonçant la bonne nouvelle dans de nombreux villages samaritains.
fr.R: Pierre et Jean ont dit aux gens ce qu’ils savaient de Jésus, et ils ont annoncé la parole du Seigneur. Puis ils sont repartis vers Jérusalem. En chemin, ils ont annoncé la bonne nouvelle dans beaucoup de villages de Samarie.

decisions.choice: having testified: having borne solemn witness
decisions.reason: The verb means to bear witness earnestly, as in 2:40. It recalls Jesus's word that his followers would be his witnesses in Samaria (1:8).

decisions.choice: they: Peter and John
decisions.reason: The sentence follows the account of Peter and John. Philip is sent on a different road in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: villages of the Samaritans: the same people John once wanted to destroy
decisions.reason: When a Samaritan village refused Jesus, James and John asked to call fire down on it (Luke 9:52-55). Now John brings the good news to Samaritan villages.

decisions.choice: Peter and John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: told people what they knew about Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what bearing witness means.

source.text: Ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν· αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος.

records.literal_gloss: An angel now of Lord spoke to Philip saying, Rise and go toward south on the road that going down from Jerusalem to Gaza; this is desert.

en.L: Now an angel of [the] Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Get up and go toward [the] south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is desert.
en.B: An angel of the Lord said to Philip, "Get ready and head south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." (This is a desert road.)
en.R: An angel from the Lord spoke to Philip. He said, "Get up and go south. Go to the road that leads down from Jerusalem to the town of Gaza." (That road goes through the desert.)

fr.L: Or un ange du Seigneur parla à Philippe, disant : « Lève-toi et va vers le midi, sur la route qui descend de Jérusalem à Gaza. » Elle est déserte.
fr.B: Un ange du Seigneur dit à Philippe : « Prépare-toi et pars vers le sud, sur la route qui descend de Jérusalem à Gaza. » (C’est une route déserte.)
fr.R: Un ange envoyé par le Seigneur a parlé à Philippe. Il lui a dit : « Lève-toi et va vers le sud. Va sur la route qui descend de Jérusalem jusqu’à la ville de Gaza. » (Cette route traverse le désert.)

decisions.choice: toward the south: the direction Philip should take
decisions.reason: The word means midday, and so also the south, where the sun stands at noon. In 22:6 it means noon. Here, with a road to follow, the direction is more likely. But a journey at noon, in the heat when few would travel, is possible.

decisions.choice: this is desert: most likely the road, which ran through lonely country
decisions.reason: "This" may point to the road or to Gaza. The old city of Gaza had been destroyed in the century before and a new city built nearby, so the words could mean the old Gaza that lay deserted. But the sentence is about the road Philip is to take, and "desert" in the sense of a lonely, empty place fits it.

decisions.choice: this is desert: a comment by Luke for his readers
decisions.reason: The words explain where the road ran. They may be the angel's, but they read more like the narrator's note.

decisions.choice: Gaza: the last town on the road south to Egypt
decisions.reason: Gaza lay near the coast in the southwest, on the route from Judea down to Egypt and on to lands further south.

decisions.choice: a desert road (B); that road goes through the desert (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading that "this" is the road, as the meaning note explains, and put the narrator's note in parentheses.

decisions.choice: the town of Gaza
decisions.reason: Readable says that Gaza was a town.

decisions.choice: vers le midi; Elle est déserte
alternatives: vers le sud; Cette route est déserte
decisions.reason: Literal keeps both open readings: "le midi" can be the south or noon (m1), and since "la route" and "Gaza" are both feminine in French, "Elle" can point to either, as the Greek pronoun can (m2). Balanced and Readable follow the reading in the meaning notes.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων, ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης αὐτῆς, ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἦν τε ὑποστρέφων καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν τὸν προφήτην Ἠσαΐαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having risen he went; and behold, a man Ethiopian, a eunuch, an official of Candace queen of Ethiopians, who was over all the treasure of her, who had come to worship to Jerusalem, \v 28 was and returning and sitting in the chariot of him and he was reading the prophet Isaiah.

en.L: And he got up and went. And look, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, an official of Candace, queen of [the] Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, who had come to Jerusalem to worship, \v 28 was returning and sitting in his chariot, and he was reading the prophet Isaiah.
en.B: So Philip got up and went. And there on the road was a man from Ethiopia, a eunuch, a high official in charge of all the treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had come to Jerusalem to worship, \v 28 and now he was on his way home, seated in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.
en.R: So Philip got up and went. On the road he saw an important man from Ethiopia, a land in Africa south of Egypt. He was a eunuch, a man who served the queen of Ethiopia. The queen was called the Candace, and this man took care of all her money. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship God. \v 28 Now he was going back home. He was sitting in his chariot and reading the book of the prophet Isaiah.

fr.L: Et, s’étant levé, il partit. Et voici, un homme éthiopien, un eunuque, haut fonctionnaire de Candace, reine des Éthiopiens, qui était [préposé] à tout son trésor, qui était venu à Jérusalem pour adorer, \v 28 était sur le retour, assis dans son char, et il lisait le prophète Isaïe.
fr.B: Philippe se leva donc et partit. Et justement, sur la route, se trouvait un Éthiopien, un eunuque, haut fonctionnaire chargé de tout le trésor de Candace, reine des Éthiopiens. Il était venu à Jérusalem pour adorer, \v 28 et maintenant il rentrait chez lui, assis dans son char, en lisant le prophète Isaïe.
fr.R: Philippe s’est donc levé et il est parti. Sur la route, il a vu un homme important qui venait d’Éthiopie, un pays d’Afrique au sud de l’Égypte. C’était un eunuque, un homme au service de la reine d’Éthiopie. On appelait la reine « la Candace », et cet homme s’occupait de tout son argent. Il était allé à Jérusalem pour adorer Dieu. \v 28 Maintenant, il rentrait chez lui. Il était assis dans son char et il lisait le livre du prophète Isaïe.

decisions.choice: Ethiopian: from the kingdom of Kush on the upper Nile, south of Egypt
alternatives: from the land now called Ethiopia
decisions.reason: The Greeks called the peoples south of Egypt Ethiopians. The kingdom Luke means had its capital at Meroë, in what is now Sudan. To Luke's readers it lay at the far edge of the known world; compare "to the end of the earth" in 1:8.

decisions.choice: eunuch: a castrated man, as many royal servants were
alternatives: simply a title for a court official
decisions.reason: The word can be a title for a high official, but here Luke has a separate word for his rank ("official"), and he goes on calling him "the eunuch". The law kept a eunuch from the assembly of the Lord (Deuteronomy 23:1), but Isaiah 56:3-5 promises eunuchs who hold to God's covenant a name better than sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: Candace: the title of the queen of Kush, not her personal name
decisions.reason: Ancient writers report that the queens, or queen mothers, of Meroë bore the title Candace (in the Meroitic language, kandake). Luke does not give the personal name of the queen.

decisions.choice: an official over all her treasure: her chief treasurer
decisions.reason: The word for official means a person of power at court. The treasure is the royal treasury.

decisions.choice: had come to worship: he worshiped the God of Israel
alternatives: he was a full convert to Judaism
decisions.reason: He had made the long journey to worship in Jerusalem and was reading the Scriptures. Luke does not say whether he was a Jew by birth, a convert, or a Gentile who worshiped God. As a eunuch he could not have entered the temple courts open to Israel.

decisions.choice: chariot: a carriage for travel
decisions.reason: The word covers any wheeled vehicle drawn by animals. He was traveling in some state, with a driver (8:38).

decisions.choice: behold: a word that points to something unexpected
decisions.reason: Luke uses it to bring a new person suddenly into view.

decisions.choice: look (L); there on the road (B); he saw (R)
decisions.reason: Modern English does not say "behold", as at 1:10.

decisions.choice: a land in Africa south of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says where Ethiopia was, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the queen was called the Candace
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Candace was a title, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: a man who served the queen
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "eunuch" and says what work he did for the queen.

decisions.choice: Et voici (L)
decisions.reason: English Literal says "look" because "behold" is no longer used; French "voici" is still current in written narrative and points to the unexpected sight as the Greek does (m7). Balanced says "Et justement, sur la route" and Readable "il a vu", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Isaïe
decisions.reason: The form used in general French and in the other French books of this translation; "Ésaïe" is the form of the Protestant tradition.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τῷ Φιλίππῳ· Πρόσελθε καὶ κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Said then the Spirit to Philip, Go near and join yourself to the chariot this.

en.L: And the Spirit said to Philip, "Go near and join this chariot."
en.B: The Spirit told Philip, "Go up to that chariot and stay with it."
en.R: The Holy Spirit said to Philip, "Go to that chariot and stay close to it."

fr.L: Et l’Esprit dit à Philippe : « Approche-toi et joins-toi à ce char. »
fr.B: L’Esprit dit à Philippe : « Va jusqu’à ce char et reste à côté. »
fr.R: L’Esprit Saint a dit à Philippe : « Va vers ce char et reste tout près. »

decisions.choice: the Spirit: the Holy Spirit, who guides Philip
decisions.reason: Luke speaks first of an angel (8:26) and now of the Spirit. The Spirit directs the mission again in 10:19, 13:2 and 16:6-7.

decisions.choice: join: keep close to, go along beside
decisions.reason: The verb means to join oneself to something. Philip is to walk or run beside the chariot; the official invites him up in 8:31.

decisions.choice: that chariot
decisions.reason: English points to something at a distance with "that".

source.text: προσδραμὼν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην καὶ εἶπεν· Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις;

records.literal_gloss: Having run up then the Philip heard him reading Isaiah the prophet and said, Then indeed do you understand what you are reading?

en.L: And Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and he said, "Do you really understand what you are reading?"
en.B: Philip ran over to him and heard him reading aloud from the prophet Isaiah. "Do you know what it is you are reading?" he asked.
en.R: Philip ran up to the chariot. He heard the man reading out loud from the prophet Isaiah. Philip asked him, "Do you understand what you are reading?"

fr.L: Et Philippe, étant accouru, l’entendit lire Isaïe le prophète, et il dit : « Comprends-tu donc ce que tu lis ? »
fr.B: Philippe accourut et l’entendit lire à haute voix le prophète Isaïe. « Comprends-tu ce que tu lis ? » lui demanda-t-il.
fr.R: Philippe a couru jusqu’au char. Il a entendu l’homme lire à voix haute le livre du prophète Isaïe. Philippe lui a demandé : « Est-ce que tu comprends ce que tu lis ? »

decisions.choice: heard him reading: he was reading aloud
decisions.reason: People in the ancient world usually read aloud, even when alone.

decisions.choice: do you understand what you are reading: a play on two related verbs, to know and to read
decisions.reason: In Greek, "understand" and "read" share a root, and the question plays on them. The opening particles show the question expects the answer "no" or invites a doubt.

decisions.choice: reading aloud (B); reading out loud (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how Philip could hear him, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: tu between Philip and the official
alternatives: vous, for a high official and a stranger
decisions.reason: The style guide follows the Greek number: "tu" to one person, "vous" to several, with no social distinction. The official also says "tu" to Philip (8:34).

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην ἐὰν μή τις ὁδηγήσει με;

records.literal_gloss: He and said, How for could I be able, if not someone will guide me?

en.L: And he said, "How could I, unless someone guides me?"
en.B: "How could I," he said, "if no one guides me?"
en.R: The man answered, "How can I understand it? I need someone to explain it to me."

fr.L: Et il dit : « Comment donc le pourrais-je, à moins que quelqu’un ne me guide ? »
fr.B: « Comment le pourrais-je, répondit-il, si personne ne me guide ? »
fr.R: L’homme a répondu : « Comment est-ce que je pourrais comprendre ? J’ai besoin que quelqu’un me l’explique. »

decisions.choice: guide: lead the way, explain
decisions.reason: The verb means to lead on the way. Jesus promised that the Spirit would guide his followers into all the truth (John 16:13).

decisions.choice: how could I: a humble admission, not a complaint
decisions.reason: The "for" ties his answer to Philip's question: no, for how could he?

decisions.choice: a question and a plain statement
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question implies.

source.text: παρεκάλεσέν τε τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: He invited then the Philip having come up to sit with him.

en.L: And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
en.B: He asked Philip to climb up and sit beside him.
en.R: So he asked Philip to come up into the chariot and sit with him.

fr.L: Et il invita Philippe à monter s’asseoir avec lui.
fr.B: Et il pria Philippe de monter s’asseoir à côté de lui.
fr.R: Alors il a demandé à Philippe de monter dans le char et de s’asseoir avec lui.

decisions.choice: invited: urged, asked earnestly
decisions.reason: The verb means to call someone alongside, to urge or invite.

decisions.choice: into the chariot
decisions.reason: Readable says where Philip came up to.

source.text: ἡ δὲ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη· Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The now passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this: As a sheep to slaughter he was led, and as a lamb before the [one] shearing him silent, so not he opens the mouth of him.

en.L: Now the passage of the Scripture that he was reading was this: "As a sheep {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was led to slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer [is] silent, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not open {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.B: The passage of Scripture he was reading was this: "Like a sheep {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was led away to be slaughtered, and like a lamb that makes no sound while it is sheared, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not open {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.R: This is the part of the Scriptures that the man was reading: "They led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away like a sheep to be killed. A lamb makes no sound when someone cuts off its wool. In the same way, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said nothing.

fr.L: Or le passage de l’Écriture qu’il lisait était celui-ci : « Comme une brebis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été conduit à l’abattoir, et comme un agneau [est] muet devant celui qui le tond, ainsi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’ouvre pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche.
fr.B: Le passage de l’Écriture qu’il lisait était celui-ci : « Comme une brebis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été emmené pour être égorgé, et comme un agneau qui reste muet quand on le tond, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a pas ouvert la bouche.
fr.R: Voici le passage des Écritures que l’homme lisait : « On {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a emmené comme un mouton qu’on va tuer. Un agneau ne fait aucun bruit quand on lui coupe sa laine. De la même façon, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a rien dit.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:7, quoted from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek of Isaiah 53:7 almost exactly. The passage is the fourth song of the servant of the Lord (Isaiah 52:13-53:12), who suffers for the sins of others.

decisions.choice: passage: the section of Scripture, the place in the scroll
decisions.reason: The word means a portion or section of a text. He was reading from a scroll of Isaiah.

decisions.choice: he does not open his mouth: he stays silent, he makes no protest
decisions.reason: Jesus kept silent before the high priest, Herod and Pilate (Luke 23:9; Mark 14:61, 15:5).

decisions.choice: he does not open: the Greek has the present tense here, after the past tense of "was led"
decisions.reason: The Greek of Isaiah mixes past and present. The sense is the same: he was silent while it was done to him.

decisions.choice: the servant's pronouns take the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: Philip tells the official that the passage speaks of Jesus (8:35). So the pronouns for the servant follow the setting for pronouns that refer to Jesus.

decisions.choice: did not open his mouth (B); said nothing (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep one tense through the picture.

decisions.choice: a lamb makes no sound when someone cuts off its wool
alternatives: as a lamb before its shearer is silent
decisions.reason: Readable says what shearing is.

decisions.choice: passé composé for the past tenses inside the quoted Scripture at every level
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The prophecy is read aloud within the story, so it takes the tenses of speech rather than of narration. Literal keeps the shift to the present in "n’ouvre pas" (m4); Balanced says "n’a pas ouvert la bouche", the French idiom, without a possessive.

source.text: ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη· τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται;

records.literal_gloss: In the humiliation the justice of him was taken away; the generation of him who will describe?

en.L: In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} humiliation {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} justice was taken away. Who will describe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} generation?
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was humiliated, justice was denied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Who can speak of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} descendants?
en.R: People treated {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with shame and did not give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a fair trial. No one can tell about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},

fr.L: Dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} humiliation, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} jugement a été enlevé. Qui racontera {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} génération ?
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été humilié, la justice {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a été refusée. Qui pourra parler de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} descendance ?
fr.R: On {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a traité avec mépris, et on ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a pas accordé un procès juste. Personne ne pourra parler de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants après {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}},

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:8, quoted from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Luke quotes the Greek of Isaiah 53:8, which reads differently from the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: his justice was taken away: he was denied a fair judgment
decisions.reason: The word means judgment. Most likely he was humiliated and robbed of justice. It can also mean that in his humiliation his sentence was lifted, that God reversed the verdict.

decisions.choice: who will describe his generation: he will have no descendants
alternatives: who can describe the wickedness of the people of his time
who can tell of his origin
decisions.reason: The word can mean descendants, the people of one's time, or one's origin. Read with the next line ("his life is taken from the earth"), it most likely means that he dies with no one to carry on his line. The question may also hint that, raised to life, he will have descendants beyond telling (Isaiah 53:10).

decisions.choice: descendants (B); children after him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading in the meaning note.

decisions.choice: did not give him a fair trial
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being denied justice means for a prisoner.

source.text: ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: For is taken from the earth the life of him.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life is taken from the earth."
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life is taken away from the earth."
en.R: because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life on earth was taken from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie est enlevée de la terre. »
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie est retranchée de la terre. »
fr.R: parce qu’on {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a pris {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie sur la terre. »

decisions.choice: his life is taken from the earth: he is put to death
alternatives: he is taken up into heaven
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as "was taken away" in the previous line. In Isaiah it describes the servant's death; in Acts it fits the death of Jesus. Some also hear in it his being lifted up from the earth.

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: Readable joins this line to the one before.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τῷ Φιλίππῳ εἶπεν· Δέομαί σου, περὶ τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει τοῦτο;

records.literal_gloss: Answering now the eunuch to Philip said, I ask you, concerning whom the prophet says this?

en.L: And the eunuch answered Philip and said, "I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this?
en.B: The eunuch said to Philip, "Please tell me, who is the prophet talking about here?
en.R: The eunuch said to Philip, "Please tell me. Who is the prophet talking about?

fr.L: Et l’eunuque, répondant, dit à Philippe : « Je t’en prie, de qui le prophète dit-il cela ?
fr.B: L’eunuque dit à Philippe : « Dis-moi, je te prie, de qui le prophète parle-t-il ici ?
fr.R: L’eunuque a dit à Philippe : « S’il te plaît, explique-moi. De qui le prophète parle-t-il ?

decisions.choice: I ask you: please, a polite request
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask or beg, used here as a courteous "please".

decisions.choice: answering: replying to the situation
decisions.reason: The participle often just introduces what someone says next.

source.text: περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ ἑτέρου τινός;

records.literal_gloss: Concerning himself or concerning other someone?

en.L: About himself or about someone else?"
en.B: Is he speaking of himself, or of another person?"
en.R: Is he talking about himself or about another man?"

fr.L: De lui-même ou de quelqu’un d’autre ? »
fr.B: Parle-t-il de lui-même, ou d’un autre ? »
fr.R: Est-ce qu’il parle de lui-même ou d’un autre homme ? »

decisions.choice: himself or someone else: who the servant is was an open question
alternatives: the question had a settled answer
decisions.reason: The servant songs do not name the servant. Elsewhere Isaiah calls Israel God's servant (Isaiah 41:8, 49:3). The official's question opens the way for Philip's answer.

source.text: ἀνοίξας δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς ταύτης εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Having opened then the Philip the mouth of him and having begun from the Scripture this he proclaimed the good news to him, the Jesus.

en.L: Then Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture he proclaimed to him the good news of Jesus.
en.B: Then Philip spoke up. Starting from that very Scripture, he made Jesus known to him as good news.
en.R: Then Philip began to speak. He started with this part of the Scriptures, and he told the man the good news about Jesus.

fr.L: Alors Philippe ouvrit la bouche et, commençant par cette Écriture, il lui annonça la bonne nouvelle de Jésus.
fr.B: Philippe prit alors la parole. Partant de ce passage même de l’Écriture, il lui fit connaître la bonne nouvelle : Jésus.
fr.R: Alors Philippe a commencé à parler. Il est parti de ce passage des Écritures, et il a annoncé à l’homme la bonne nouvelle de Jésus.

decisions.choice: opened his mouth: began to speak at length
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the start of a solemn speech (10:34, Matthew 5:2). It also echoes the servant who "did not open his mouth" (8:32).

decisions.choice: beginning from this Scripture: the servant is Jesus
alternatives: Philip spoke of Jesus apart from the passage
decisions.reason: Philip begins with Isaiah 53 and shows that it speaks of Jesus. The risen Jesus did the same with the Scriptures for his disciples (Luke 24:27, 24:44-47).

decisions.choice: proclaimed Jesus as good news: Jesus himself was the content of the good news
decisions.reason: The verb for announcing good news takes "Jesus" as its object, as in 5:42.

decisions.choice: spoke up
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English phrase; Literal keeps the idiom.

decisions.choice: prit la parole
decisions.reason: "Prendre la parole" is the natural French for beginning to speak at length (m1), as the English Balanced "spoke up"; Literal keeps the idiom.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ, καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος· Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ, τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: As then they were going along the road, they came upon some water, and says the eunuch, Look, water; what prevents me to be baptized?

en.L: And as they were going along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch says, "Look, water! What prevents me from being baptized?"
en.B: As they traveled on along the road, they came to some water. "There is water here!" the eunuch exclaimed. "Is there any reason I should not be baptized?"
en.R: As they went along the road, they came to a place with some water. The eunuch said, "Look! Here is some water! Is there any reason I cannot be baptized?"

fr.L: Et comme ils allaient le long de la route, ils arrivèrent à un point d’eau, et l’eunuque dit : « Voici de l’eau ! Qu’est-ce qui m’empêche d’être baptisé ? »
fr.B: Comme ils poursuivaient leur route, ils arrivèrent près d’un point d’eau. « Il y a de l’eau ici ! s’écria l’eunuque. Y a-t-il une raison pour que je ne sois pas baptisé ? »
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils avançaient sur la route, ils sont arrivés à un endroit où il y avait de l’eau. L’eunuque a dit : « Regarde ! Il y a de l’eau ici ! Est-ce que quelque chose m’empêche d’être baptisé ? »

decisions.choice: what prevents me: is there anything to stop me
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "nothing". The same verb is used when Peter asks whether anyone can prevent the baptism of Cornelius's household (10:47; compare 11:17). The man the law kept out (Deuteronomy 23:1) asks what keeps him out now.

decisions.choice: says: a vivid present tense in a past narrative
decisions.reason: Greek often uses the present tense to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT has no verse 37
decisions.reason: Verse 37 is missing from the earliest and most important manuscripts and is not in the SBLGNT. It is found in later manuscripts, in some forms of the old Latin, and in the King James Version. In it Philip says he may be baptized if he believes with all his heart, and the eunuch answers that he believes that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. It looks like an early baptismal confession added to the story. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: said (R), exclaimed (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the past tense of the story.

source.text: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα, καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος, καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And he ordered to stop the chariot, and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

en.L: And he ordered the chariot to stop, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
en.B: He gave orders to halt the chariot, and the two of them, Philip and the eunuch, went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
en.R: The eunuch told the driver to stop the chariot. Philip and the eunuch both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

fr.L: Et il ordonna que le char s’arrête, et ils descendirent tous deux dans l’eau, Philippe et l’eunuque, et il le baptisa.
fr.B: Il fit arrêter le char ; tous deux, Philippe et l’eunuque, descendirent dans l’eau, et Philippe le baptisa.
fr.R: L’eunuque a dit au conducteur d’arrêter le char. Philippe et l’eunuque sont descendus tous les deux dans l’eau, et Philippe l’a baptisé.

decisions.choice: he ordered: the official gave the command to his driver
decisions.reason: The official is the one with servants under him. The subject of "baptized" is Philip.

decisions.choice: went down into the water: they stepped into the water for the baptism
decisions.reason: The phrase says they went down into the water and came up out of it (8:39). It does not describe how the baptism was done.

decisions.choice: Philip baptized him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who did the baptizing, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the eunuch told the driver
decisions.reason: Readable names who gave the order and to whom.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος, πνεῦμα κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον, καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος, ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων.

records.literal_gloss: When now they came up out of the water, [the] Spirit of Lord carried away the Philip, and not saw him no longer the eunuch, he went for the way of him rejoicing.

en.L: And when they came up out of the water, [the] Spirit of [the] Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no longer, for he went on his way rejoicing.
en.B: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away. The eunuch did not see him again, but he traveled on with a glad heart.
en.R: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away. The eunuch never saw Philip again. But he went on his way home, full of joy.

fr.L: Et quand ils furent remontés de l’eau, l’Esprit du Seigneur enleva Philippe, et l’eunuque ne le vit plus, car il poursuivait son chemin en se réjouissant.
fr.B: Quand ils furent sortis de l’eau, l’Esprit du Seigneur emporta soudain Philippe. L’eunuque ne le revit plus, mais il continua sa route, le cœur plein de joie.
fr.R: Quand ils sont sortis de l’eau, l’Esprit du Seigneur a tout à coup emmené Philippe. L’eunuque n’a plus jamais revu Philippe. Mais il a repris la route de chez lui, plein de joie.

decisions.choice: snatched away: took away suddenly and by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to seize or carry off. Obadiah fears the Spirit of the Lord will carry Elijah away (1 Kings 18:12; compare 2 Kings 2:16). Paul uses it of being caught up to the third heaven (2 Corinthians 12:2).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away"
alternatives: "the Holy Spirit fell on the eunuch, and an angel of the Lord snatched Philip away"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, mainly of the Western text, say the Holy Spirit fell on the eunuch and an angel of the Lord took Philip away. The shorter reading is better attested. The longer one may have been added to show that the eunuch too received the Spirit. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: for he went on his way rejoicing: the eunuch did not stay to look for Philip
alternatives: he never saw him because he left
decisions.reason: The "for" explains why the eunuch saw Philip no more: he did not stay but went on his road home, glad.

decisions.choice: rejoicing: glad, full of joy
decisions.reason: Joy follows the coming of salvation in Acts (8:8, 13:48, 16:34).

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: English shows the link more naturally with a contrast; the reason is clear from the story.

source.text: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον, καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν.

records.literal_gloss: Philip however was found at Azotus, and passing through he was proclaiming the good news to the towns all until the coming him to Caesarea.

en.L: But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through, he proclaimed the good news to all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
en.B: Philip, for his part, turned up at Azotus. He went on through the region, announcing the good news in every town until he reached Caesarea.
en.R: Later Philip found himself in the town of Azotus. He traveled through that area and told the good news about Jesus in all the towns. He did this until he came to the city of Caesarea.

fr.L: Mais Philippe fut trouvé à Azot, et, traversant [la région], il annonçait la bonne nouvelle à toutes les villes, jusqu’à ce qu’il arrive à Césarée.
fr.B: Philippe, quant à lui, se retrouva à Azot. Il traversa la région en annonçant la bonne nouvelle dans toutes les villes, jusqu’à son arrivée à Césarée.
fr.R: Plus tard, Philippe s’est retrouvé dans la ville d’Azot. Il a voyagé dans toute cette région et il a annoncé la bonne nouvelle de Jésus dans toutes les villes. Il a fait cela jusqu’à son arrivée dans la ville de Césarée.

decisions.choice: Azotus: the Greek name of Ashdod, on the coast north of Gaza
decisions.reason: Ashdod was one of the old Philistine cities (1 Samuel 5:1). From there the coast road runs north to Caesarea.

decisions.choice: Caesarea: the port city built by Herod, seat of the Roman governors
decisions.reason: This is Caesarea on the coast. Philip still lives there years later (21:8).

decisions.choice: was found at: appeared, turned up at
decisions.reason: The passive form is used for someone who arrives unexpectedly at a place, as in the Greek of 1 Kings 18:12.

decisions.choice: the good news about Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names what the good news was about, as in 8:35.

decisions.choice: Azot
decisions.reason: The usual French form of the Greek name of Ashdod (m1).
